- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in the early days of the forecast horizon.
- Forecasts peak too early and overshoot the true price trajectory, particularly after sharp spikes in the history.
- Model fails to account for mean reversion in the later half of the forecast, underestimating sharp declines after peaks.
- Forecast bias is stronger when the history contains recent high values; model reacts too aggressively to recent spikes.
- Model does not adjust for the lag between historical data and true outcome, especially when true values rise sharply after the forecast window begins.
- Overshoot correction needed after any spike in history: reduce forecast by 5–10% for the next 3–5 days.
- Mean reversion rule: if true outcome drops below 10% of the forecast peak, reduce forecast by 2–5% per day until convergence.
- Horizon-specific: for forecasts beyond 10 days, apply a 2–3% downward adjustment to avoid overconfidence in long-term growth.
